note: All configuration is the config object adv_varnish.cache_settings (sections general.*, available.*, cache_control.*), edited at /admin/config/development/adv_varnish. Cache invalidation goes through adv_varnish.cache_manager (tagged cache_tags_invalidator), which sends HTTP BAN requests to general.varnish_server but only when general.varnish_purger is TRUE. The module defines a user_blocks plugin type (namespace Plugin/UserBlocks, base UserBlockBase) for ESI per-user fragments. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the real adv_varnish.cache_settings config object (no live Varnish server is contacted). Scripts write/read config via the config API; cleanup/reset restore the shipped install default (only cache_control.anonymous set).

evals.prompt: In the Advanced Varnish cache (adv_varnish) Drupal module, which config object holds all settings, at what admin path do you edit them, and which setting is the master switch that turns Varnish caching on?
evals.expected_output: Config object adv_varnish.cache_settings, edited at /admin/config/development/adv_varnish (route adv_varnish.config_form). The master switch is available.enable_cache.

evals.prompt: How does adv_varnish invalidate cached content on the Varnish server when Drupal cache tags change, and which setting must be on for it to happen?
evals.expected_output: The adv_varnish.cache_manager service (tagged cache_tags_invalidator) turns cache-tag invalidations into HTTP BAN requests to the configured varnish_server, but only when general.varnish_purger is enabled.

evals.prompt: adv_varnish supports keeping per-user page fragments dynamic while the page is cached. What plugin type does it define for this, and where do such plugins live / what base class do they extend?
evals.expected_output: It defines the user_blocks plugin type (manager plugin.manager.user_blocks). Plugins live in a module's Plugin/UserBlocks namespace, extend UserBlockBase (implement UserBlocksInterface, tagged with the UserBlocks attribute), and provide per-user content served via ESI.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Advanced Varnish cache has been pointed at a Varnish server. Inspect the live adv_varnish.cache_settings config and report the configured Varnish server host.
evals.expected_output: The Varnish server is http://varnish.mdtest:6081: adv_varnish.cache_settings general.varnish_server = 'http://varnish.mdtest:6081'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Advanced Varnish cache has a page cache TTL configured. Inspect the live adv_varnish.cache_settings config and report the configured page cache maximum age (in seconds).
evals.expected_output: The page cache maximum age is 900: adv_varnish.cache_settings general.page_cache_maximum_age = '900'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use Advanced Varnish cache to turn on Varnish caching (the master enable switch). Apply the change to the live adv_varnish.cache_settings configuration.
evals.expected_output: adv_varnish.cache_settings available.enable_cache = true (e.g. drush cset adv_varnish.cache_settings available.enable_cache 1, or tick 'Enable Varnish cache' on the settings form).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Advanced Varnish cache to send purge requests to the Varnish server at http://varnish.example.com:6081 and enable the built-in Varnish purger. Apply the change to the live adv_varnish.cache_settings configuration.
